title: Hypothesis-driven Sentinel for Rollback after Config Shifts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We frequently change model configs (quantization profile, kernel selection, batching) and deploy model variants. Current staged rollouts rely on fixed metric thresholds and simple moving averages which either (a) false-positive rollback noisy experiments, or (b) miss subtle quality regressions introduced by config/model shifts. Goal: implement a hypothesis-driven sentinel service that attaches to canary and A/B rollouts, runs sequential statistical tests across multiple signal types (quality, semantic drift, hallucination proxy), and triggers automatic mitigation policies when a prespecified hypothesis is rejected. The sentinel should produce explainable decision artifacts for SRE/PM/Design review and support human-in-the-loop hold for marginal cases.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel can be attached to any rollout or config flip via rollout config and starts evaluating within first 5 minutes of exposure
Support for at least three signal categories: fidelity (QA-style eval set pass rate), semantic drift (embedding distance distribution shift), and hallucination proxy (unanswerable rate)
Sequential hypothesis testing with configurable alpha and burn-in guarantees false positive rate <= configured alpha over run duration
Automated mitigation policy options implemented: traffic throttle to baseline, model-variant fallback, and config revert with a single API call
Decision artifacts include: test statistic time-series, sample-level examples triggering the alert, and recommended rollback reason; artifacts persisted to the rollout trace and visible in Console
E2E test harness with synthetic drift generator that validates rollback occurs on known regressions within target latency and with low false positives
Docs and runbook published and product reviewed by SRE/PM/Design
Telemetry: measurable reduction in customer-facing regressions during internal canaries in 2-week pilot

implementation_notes: Architecture: sentinel will be a control-plane microservice that subscribes to rollout events. For each rollout it will spawn a lightweight evaluation session: 1) stream aggregated metrics from runtime telemetry (latency, token-level error proxies), 2) sample-level pull from storage for targeted evals (QA prompts, hallucination probes), 3) compute sequential test statistics for each signal and run a multivariate decision rule that accounts for correlation. Decision rules: default is two-stage: (A) rapid detection via CUSUM on aggregated quality score, (B) confirmatory Bayesian posterior on sampled examples. Mitigation connector: call rollout API to apply one of three policies: throttle, variant-fallback, full config revert. Data retention: keep decision artifacts for 90 days. Operational concerns: quota for sampling, backpressure if rollout traffic is huge, and privacy constraints for PII in saved sample artifacts.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (monitor-only): attach sentinel to internal feature flags and run for 2 weeks with no auto-mitigations. Phase 2 (pilot auto-mitigations): enable auto-throttle + variant-fallback for non-critical customers for 1 week. Phase 3 (gradual rollout): enable full auto-revert for internal and low-risk customers, iterate on thresholds. Phase 4: general availability with runbook and dashboards.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High false positive rate causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative alpha by default, human-in-the-loop hold when borderline, and monitor FPR in pilot
Risk: Runtime overhead for sampling. Mitigation: sample at 0.1% by default and prioritize edge cases via waterfall sampling
Risk: Missing subtle but critical regressions that don't surface in our eval sets. Mitigation: allow customer-provided eval sets and augment with adversarial prompt generators
Risk: Privacy exposure in persisted samples. Mitigation: PII scrubber pipeline and policy to redact or exclude user-provided data
